extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in discrete geometry and sphere-packing (readers of Hales' proof of the Kepler conjecture)
extracted.subtask_description: Establish local optimality of the score function σ on the space of decomposition stars DS; show that σ ≤ 8·pt with equality only for the face-centered cubic or hexagonal-close packings, and that quad clusters and other standard clusters satisfy specified score bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of volume and score components
rubrics_metrics.description: The maps D ↦ vol Ω(D), the terms vol VC(S, v), s-vor(S, v), and the composed function σ(S, c, v) (when viewed on the appropriate components of the decomposition-star space DS) are continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: σ is not continuous as a function of the set of quarters because of case breakings at certain circumradius thresholds (e.g., 1.41 and √2). Those cutoffs are incorporated into the data indexing decomposition stars (I8, I9) so that different cases fall in different connected components of DS, restoring continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 5.10 (A1 cancellation for simplices in S-system)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S = {v1,v2,v3,v4} a simplex in the S-system with context c, the combined A1-terms satisfy ∑_{i=1}^{4} A1(S,c,vi) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently (by Formula 5.5) ∑_{i=1}^{4} σ(S,c,vi) = ∑_{i=1}^{4} s-vor(S,c,vi). The s-vor0 terms cancel pairwise and other terms are weighted averages, so the sum is unchanged by averaging—hence the identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negligibility (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function A : Λ → R is negligible if there exists a constant C1 such that for all r ≥ 1, ∑_{v ∈ Λ(x,r)} A(v) ≤ C1·r^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Definition 1.2 recalled here and is the key growth bound used to show the corrective function A does not affect asymptotic density arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of A(v) from local decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A(v) is defined by A(v) = A0(D(v,Λ)), where A0 depends on A1 and σ via Equations 5.2, 5.5 and Definition 5.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The negligibility and compatibility properties of A are studied by analyzing these local contributions coming from decomposition stars around each vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.11 (A is negligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function A defined by A(v)=A0(D(v,Λ)) is negligible (satisfies the r^2 growth bound).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: first treat simplified A'(v)=−vol(Ω(D(v,Λ))) + vol(VC(D(v,Λ))) and bound its sum by comparing balls containing Voronoi and V-cells. Then include A1-sums and use Lemma 5.10 to show massive cancellation (quarters occur four times), leaving only boundary contributions bounded by O(r^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.12 (score σ of a decomposition star)
rubrics_metrics.description: σ(D) = −4·δ_oct·(vol Ω(D) + A0(D)) + 16π/3; this quantity is called the score of the decomposition star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rescaled version of A and Voronoi volume is the primary function whose maxima/minima determine fcc-compatibility and optimality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence for fcc-compatibility (Lemma 5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are equivalent: (1) The minimum over DS of D ↦ vol Ω(D) + A0(D) is 32. (2) The maximum of σ on DS is 8·pt. Moreover, these imply that for every saturated packing Λ, the function A is fcc-compatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus proving σ(D) ≤ 8·pt for all D ∈ DS (and characterizing equality) is equivalent to establishing the required fcc-compatibility of the corrective function A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.14 (implication to existence of negligible fcc-compatible A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the maximum of σ on DS is 8·pt, then for every saturated packing Λ there exists a negligible fcc-compatible function A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine Theorem 5.11 (negligibility) and Lemma 5.13 (equivalence) to produce the desired function A for any saturated packing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard cluster decomposition of σ (Equation 5.7 and Defs 5.15–5.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: σ(D) decomposes as σ(D) = Σ_R σ_R(D) where the sum runs over standard clusters (R,D). For measurable R, vor_R(D) = 4(−δ_oct·vol VCR(D) + sol(R)/3) and σ_R(D) = vor_R(D) − 4δ_oct·Σ_{Q ∈ Q0(R,D)} A1(Q,c(Q,D),0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses the global score as a sum of regional scores attached to standard regions, which allows local analysis per cluster/region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 5.18 (local linear relation for σ_R)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R' is the part of a standard region R not lying in the cone over any Q ∈ Q0(R,D), then σ_R(D) = vor_{R'}(D) + Σ_{Q ∈ Q0(R,D)} σ(Q,c(Q,D),0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains why the same symbol σ is used for both σ_R(D) and σ(Q,c,v): the region score splits into a Voronoi-type term plus the cluster scores of simplices lying in the cone over R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local optimality theorem (Theorem 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D be a contravening decomposition star with U(D) (sphere-packing vectors within distance ≤ 2t0 from origin) having twelve elements and whose proximity graph is isomorphic (via a bijection ψ) to the contact graph of the twelve-ball kissing arrangement of the fcc or hcp packing. Then σ(D) ≤ 8·pt. Equality holds iff U(D) coincides with the fcc or hcp kissing arrangement up to Euclidean motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a local characterization of maxima: the only local maxima achieving 8·pt correspond to the fcc/hcp kissing configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.3 (graph-based local optimality)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contravening decomposition star D has plane graph isomorphic to G_fcc or G_hcp then σ(D) = 8·pt and, up to Euclidean motion, U(D) is the standard kissing arrangement of fcc or hcp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent restatement of Theorem 6.1 once plane graphs G(D) are formally introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.4 (quad cluster and other cluster score bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quad cluster scores at most 0; equality occurs only for a quad cluster whose corners have height 2 and form a square of side 2. All other standard clusters have strictly negative scores: σ_R(D) < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key ingredient: six quad clusters in the fcc/hcp vertex neighborhood have nonpositive score, eight quasi-regular tetrahedra score ≤ 1·pt (≤ equality only for regular tetrahedron of side 2), summing to ≤ 8·pt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rogers simplex density monotonicity (Lemma 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Rogers simplex R(a,b,c) (1 ≤ a < b < c) with distinguished vertex at origin, A(a,b,c)/vol(R(a,b,c)) (where A is volume of intersection with unit ball) is monotonically decreasing in each variable a,b,c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rogers' lemma is used to compare densities of Rogers simplices occurring in Voronoi-type decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Rogers simplex bound (Lemma 6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Rogers simplex R(a,b,√2) with 1 ≤ a ≤ b and η(2,2,2) ≤ b ≤ √2, the intersection volume A with B(0,1) satisfies A ≤ δ_oct·vol(R(a,b,√2)), with equality only if a=1 and b=η(2,2,2) or simplex is degenerate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to bound densities in pieces of V-cells arising in quarters and related solids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedge density bound (Lemma 6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For wedge W(α,z0)= {t x: 0≤t≤1, x∈P(α,z0)} with z0 ≥1 and P(α,z0) as given, the intersection A with B(0,1) satisfies A ≤ δ_oct·vol(W). Equality only if W has zero volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to conic wedge pieces that appear when decomposing V-cells around certain simplices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cone density bound (Lemma 6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is the cone at origin over P where every point of P has distance at least 1.18 from origin, and A is volume of intersection C∩B(0,1), then A ≤ δ_oct·vol(C). Equality only if C has zero volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show parts of V-cells whose directions are bounded away from origin have density strictly less than δ_oct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-regular tetrahedron score bound (Lemma 6.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasi-regular tetrahedron S satisfies σ(S) ≤ 1·pt, with equality iff S is a regular tetrahedron of edge length 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a verified (computer) inequality (calc-586468779) used to bound contributions of tetrahedral standard clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarter score bound (Lemma 6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any quarter Q in the Q-system satisfies σ(Q) ≤ 0. Equality occurs iff five edges have length 2 and the diagonal has length √8 (the extremal quarter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof splits into contexts (upright, flat) and uses several verified inequalities (cited calculations) plus density decompositions of VC(Q,v) into Rogers simplices, wedges and cones applying Lemmas 6.6–6.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplex s-vor negativity (Lemma 6.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a simplex all of whose faces have circumradius ≤ √2 and S is not a quasi-regular tetrahedron or quarter, then s-vor(S) < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses monotonicity of circumradius and Rogers lemma to show densities in constituent Rogers simplices are < δ_oct, hence s-vor negative; verified by computer-assisted inequalities in listed domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-overlap criterion for small triangles vs barriers (Lemma 6.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a triangle of circumradius < √2 and none of its edges passes through a barrier in B, then T does not overlap any barrier in B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edge non-intersection ensures full non-overlap by earlier Lemma 2.21; used to classify simplices that belong to Q0' versus those that interact with barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangle hitting a barrier (Lemma 6.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T = {u,v,w} has circumradius < √2 and an edge {v,w} passes through a barrier b = {v1,v2,v3}, then: (i) edge {v,w} has length between 2t0 and √8; (ii) u is a vertex of b; (iii) one endpoint y∈{v,w} satisfies {y,v1,v2,v3} ∈ Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides necessary structural constraints when triangles intersect barriers, used in combinatorial/geometry case distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation lemmas for cones (Lemmas 6.17 and 6.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.17: For v of height ≤ √(8) (?) and v2,v3 satisfying certain distinctness and η(0,v2,v3) < √2, the open cone at origin over B(0,√2)∩B(v,√2) does not meet closed cone at origin over convex hull of {v2,v3}. Lemma 6.18: Similar non-intersection when v1 has height ≤ 2t0 and {0,v2,v3} is a barrier and {0,v1,v2,v3} ∉ Q0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geometric separation facts are used to show local pieces (cones) do not overlap the cones of certain simplices or barriers, enabling partitioning of VC(0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended Q0' definition (Definition 6.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q0' is the set of simplices S with vertex at origin such that either S∈Q0, or S has vertex at origin, circumradius < √2, and none of its edges passes through a barrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enlarged set is used to partition and analyze VC(0) into non-overlapping simplices and residual regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-overlap of simplices in Q0' (Lemma 6.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplices in Q0' do not overlap one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows because Q0 simplices don't overlap and edges of simplices in Q0' don't pass through barriers or edges of Q0, so there can be no overlap (uses Lemma 2.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of C'(v) (Definition 6.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For |v| ≤ 2.36 define C'(v) as subset of cone C(v) (the cone from origin over B(v,√2)∩B(0,√2)) satisfying six conditions: (1) x∈C(v); (2) x closer to 0 than to v; (3) x∈B(0,√2); (4) x not in cone over any simplex in Q0; (5) for any u≠0,v with {0,u,v} a barrier or circumradius <√2 and edges not passing through barrier, x and v lie in same half-space bounded by plane perpendicular to {0,u,v} through 0 and circumcenter; (6) for any {0,v1,v2,v}∈Q0, segment {x,v} does not cross cone C({0,v1,v2}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C'(v) isolates the part of VC(0) near the direction of v that is closer to 0 than to v and avoids cones over Q0 simplices and barrier-induced separations; it's the basic unit used in the density partitioning argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: C'(v) subset of VC(0) (Lemma 6.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every vertex v with |v| ≤ 2.36, we have C'(v) ⊂ VC(0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses obstruction and barrier-case analysis: any point x∈C'(v) that were closer to some other u would contradict conditions (5)–(6) or barrier geometry, thus x must be in VC(0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Star-convexity and face relation (Lemma 6.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F(v) be the Voronoi face Ω(0)∩Ω(v); let F'(v) be part of F(v)∩B(0,1.18) not in cone over any simplex in Q0; let H(v) be closure of union of segments from origin to F'(v); let C''(v) be cone spanned by B(0,1.18)∩B(v,1.18). Then closure of C'(v) ∩ C''(v) equals H(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relates geometric cones C' to Voronoi faces and shows the C' regions capture the radial sweep to the portions of the Voronoi face not covered by Q0 cones; used to argue partitioning and density estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage lemma (Corollary 6.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x ∈ VC(0) with 0<|x|≤1.18, and the point at distance 1.18 along ray (0,x) is not in VC(0), and x is not in cone over any simplex of Q0, then there exists v with x∈C'(v) and |v| ≤ 2.36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides that residual points of VC(0) (not in Q0 cones) belong to some C'(v), enabling exhaustive partitioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disjointness of C'(u) and C'(v) (Lemma 6.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If |u| ≤ 2.36 and |v| ≤ 2.36 and u ≠ v, then C'(u) and C'(v) do not overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If overlap occurred, circumradius of {0,u,v} ≤ √2 and either separation plane (no barrier edge) or barrier arguments prevent the overlap; used to ensure partition components are disjoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barrier-edge propagation (Lemma 6.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a simplex with circumradius < √2 and five of its six edges do not pass through a barrier, then the sixth edge also does not pass through a barrier unless both endpoints of the opposite edge are vertices of the barrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to eliminate certain partially-barrier-crossing simplex configurations when building Q0' and partitioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: σ_R(D) ≤ 0 for non-triangular standard regions (Lemma 6.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a standard region that is not a triangle, then σ_R(D) ≤ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: partition VC(D) by Q0 and Q0' cones and the C'(v) regions; show each piece has density ≤ δ_oct by applying Lemmas 6.5–6.8 and prior simplex/quarter/tetrahedron score bounds; parts corresponding to Q0 simplices handled by Lemmas 6.10, 6.12, and non-Q0' pieces by Lemma 6.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of equality for non-triangular regions (Lemma 6.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a standard region that is not a triangle and σ_R(D) = 0, then (R,D) is a quad cluster whose four corners have height 2 and form a square of side 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pins down the only case of zero score among non-triangular standard regions: the ideal quad cluster in the fcc/hcp configuration; combines prior inequalities and equality case analyses of the local density bounds.
